messages:
joanna: deploy-bot just flagged PR #4825 — small runtime config tweak in runtime/config/defaults.yaml. It suggested an automatic patch bump (no API surface change). Thoughts on pin vs caret and whether this should be patch-only?

deploy-bot: Automated change detection:
- Files: runtime/config/defaults.yaml
- Change: default_seq_len: 2048 -> 1536
- Suggested semver: patch
- Suggested tag: v1.8.3
Suggested deploy command:
```
git tag -a v1.8.3 -m "runtime: adjust default_seq_len to reduce latency spikes"
/deploy --tag v1.8.3
```
Note: No code-level API changes detected.

michael: If it's just a default tweak then patch seems appropriate. One ask: add a clear release-note about perf/cost impact and run a staging canary first. Default changes can affect tail latency.

sasha: Agree patch. Also to be explicit: this is not a dependency pin or npm/package.json change, right? (those should be handled separately)

joanna: Correct — no dep changes. It's an internal perf knob. Plan proposal: patch bump + rc canary. Release note line: "tune default seq len to reduce latency spikes". Schedule for tonight's change window at 02:00 UTC. Any objections?

ops-oncall: No objections, but require a canary at 10% for 15m with alert hooks on p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate. If any regression, immediate rollback. Recommend tag flow: v1.8.3-rc1 for canary, then v1.8.3 for full.

kevin: For rollback we should decide: revert commit vs rollback tag. My preference: create a revert PR and publish next patch (v1.8.4) if we need to go back — keeps history clean. Rollback tags are faster though if we need immediate mitigation.

michael: Deploy-bot supports both rollback-tag and revert+patch flows. For speed in an incident, rollback-tag is fine. For postmortem/cleanliness, revert+new-patch is better. So: use rollback-tag for hotfix if needed, then follow up with revert PR and bump.

sasha: Sounds good. I'll prep the changelog entry and QA checklist: https://go/rel/4825-checklist (contains perf dashboards to validate).

joanna: Ok going to merge + create v1.8.3-rc1 tag for canary. deploy-bot, please tag and schedule canary at 02:00 UTC. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Queued: tagging and scheduling canary. Example scheduled command (internal ops use):
```
git tag -a v1.8.3-rc1 -m "canary: runtime default_seq_len tweak"
/deploy schedule --channel canary --tag v1.8.3-rc1 --time 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z --percent 10 --duration 15m
```
Will post status updates when canary starts and after 15m. If ops-oncall triggers rollback, will execute rollback flow as requested.

joanna: Thanks all — will follow up with the release-note snippet and link to PR."
